apps.name: Dylan's Baritone Ukulele
apps.subtitle: Chords and notes for baritone uke
description: A baritone ukulele (tuned D G B E, like a guitar's top four strings) that you play with your finger. Tap spots on the neck to press the strings: it plays each note and tells you, in plain English, which chord you've made.
Below the neck are 21 common chords and every note the neck can play. Tap one to hear it, see how to finger it, and put it on the neck.
features: A neck you can press, with a real plucked-string sound
Names any chord you make ("G major chord, bright and happy")
21 chords with finger-by-finger steps
Every note on the staff, and everywhere it's played on the neck
Works without internet

apps.name: Dylan's Bassoon
apps.subtitle: An interactive bassoon fingering chart
description: Every key and hole of a German-system bassoon, both hands, front and back. Tap them to press them (as many as you like) and it tells you which note that plays, or what's closest if it isn't a real fingering.
Or go the other way: pick any note from low B♭ to high D and see exactly how to finger it, in a picture and in plain words, with the other common ways to play it.
features: All 42 notes, from low B♭ to high D, in bass and tenor clef
Press the keys yourself and see what note you get
Half-holes, flick keys and other ways to play each note
Fingerings checked against the International Double Reed Society's chart

apps.name: Dylan's Weather App
apps.subtitle: Live radar and the forecast, at a glance
description: A live, animated weather radar in a soft Windy-style look, with the last hour of rain playing on a loop. Below it: the weather right now, any alerts, the chance of rain hour by hour for the next three days (colored like the radar, with when to expect rain each day), and the 7-day forecast.
It starts on Fort Lauderdale. Tap the place's name to pick yours, or use where you are. Your place stays on your phone. US places only: the forecast and radar come from the National Weather Service.

apps.name: Dylan's Daily Torah
apps.subtitle: This week's portion, a section a day
description: This week's Torah portion in English and Hebrew: what happens in it, its four main lessons, and its haftarah.

Then today's section of it: an insight to take into the day, the verse of the day in Hebrew and English, and Rashi on it. Then the Talmud on today's verse: a Mishnah and a passage of the Gemara, each in the original, in English, and in plain English. Every text has a link to read it on Sefaria.
Last, where the portion falls among all 54, and the Hebrew year as a wheel with the moon and the holidays coming up.

Below it, the whole periodic table with today's element lit up and the ones you've already seen this round shaded, every family in its own pastel color.

apps.name: Dylan's Tarot
apps.subtitle: Learn to read tarot, in plain English
description: A tarot teacher in your pocket, with seven decks to choose from: the classic 1909 Rider-Waite-Smith deck, old French and Italian decks, and the Sola Busca of 1491, the oldest complete tarot in the world. Draw a card of the day, lay out a reading and see it read the way a teacher would: each card in its spot, what stands out across the table, famous pairs, and the story put together.

Twelve short lessons take you from the very basics to reading for someone else, and every one of the 78 cards is explained in plain English: what it means right side up and upside down, what's in the picture, and a trick for remembering it.

apps.name: Dylan's Corkboard
apps.subtitle: South Florida events, and your own reminders
description: A cork board with pages torn off notepads, one page per month. The first board is things to do around South Florida: Greater Fort Lauderdale's big yearly events (the boat show, Winterfest, Tortuga, the air show and more), the Las Olas art fairs, Art Basel, the Delray Affair, nights out, Halloween Horror Nights and IBJJF jiu-jitsu tournaments, with a map showing where each one is and the farmers markets of the week.
Hold an event for a moment and let go to add it to your calendar.
The second board is yours: add your appointments, reminders and birthdays, and they land on the right month's page. They stay on your phone.

apps.name: Dylan's Athletics

description: Run clubs, archery and pickleball around Fort Lauderdale: every weekly group run (today's first), Fort Lauderdale Archers, Gold Coast Archers, FAU's archery club and Markham Park's public range, and The Fort and the city's free pickleball courts. Tap any of them for driving directions.

Every weekend jiu-jitsu open mat from Jupiter down to Miami and out west, on a cork board: a map with a numbered pin for each gym, and a Saturday paper and a Sunday paper listing every open mat by time.
